recognize_zh: 黏液胭脂紅（mucicarmine）染色下，淋巴球整體呈紅色，但細胞邊緣的球形包涵體保持蒼白、未被染成紅色，表示包涵體不含黏液（mucin）；背景的小紅點為血小板。
features: Small round lymphocytes stained diffusely red-magenta by the carmine/counterstain
Pale, unstained globular cytoplasmic inclusions at the cell periphery, singly or in small groups
No carmine-positive (mucin) material within the inclusions
Numerous small scattered red-stained platelets; green arrow indicates a small platelet-sized particle next to a lymphocyte
Red cells are faint ghost outlines in the background
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear stained with mucicarmine shows small lymphocytes containing pale, globular cytoplasmic inclusions that fail to take up the carmine stain. No mucin-positive material is identified within the inclusions. Scattered platelets are present, and red cells appear only as faint outlines. Findings indicate that the cytoplasmic inclusions in these CLL lymphocytes are mucin-negative.

ddx.vs: Signet-ring cells contain mucicarmine-positive mucin vacuoles and are large epithelial cells, not small lymphocytes.
Lipid vacuoles stain with Oil Red O and are seen in neutrophils and monocytes as well, whereas these inclusions are confined to lymphocytes.
Immunoglobulin globules are typically PAS-positive and demonstrate light-chain restriction by immunocytochemistry, which separates them from stain-negative inclusions.
Storage-disease vacuoles are multiple small punched-out vacuoles in otherwise normal lymphocytes and may stain with PAS or toluidine blue, unlike the large globules here.
